title: GPIO overview: output type, input bias and reset state
summary: Choose push-pull or open-drain behavior and define input bias before layout. Review voltage compatibility, reset states and loading.
applies_to: Digital GPIO circuits; pin capabilities and electrical limits require the selected device datasheet.
required_inputs: Pin modes, supply sequence and receiver thresholds
verification: Check pin electrical limits and reset configuration against the exact datasheet.
limitations: GPIO labels alone do not establish tolerance, available current or powered-off behavior.

title: GPIO push-pull point-to-point pattern
summary: Connect one push-pull driver to a compatible input; check input transition requirements under the actual load.
applies_to: Digital GPIO circuits; pin capabilities and electrical limits require the selected device datasheet.
required_inputs: VOH/VOL, VIH/VIL, input capacitance and edge limits
verification: Check loaded logic levels, edge shape and startup behavior.
limitations: Do not assume that slower edges always improve operation.

title: GPIO open-drain shared interrupt pattern
summary: Share an active-low interrupt only among compatible open-drain outputs. Size the pull-up for the combined load and sink capability.
applies_to: Digital GPIO circuits; pin capabilities and electrical limits require the selected device datasheet.
required_inputs: Pull-up rail, leakage, capacitance and receiver timing
verification: Verify the released HIGH and asserted LOW with every participant and power state.
limitations: Internal pull-ups and unpowered-device tolerance are device-specific.

title: STM32 device note: GPIO speed and unused pins
summary: Use AN4899 alongside the exact STM32 datasheet for output speed, unused-pin configuration and low-power states.
applies_to: STM32 MCUs covered by AN4899; confirm the exact device, pin and low-power mode in its datasheet and reference manual.
required_inputs: STM32 part, pin type and low-power mode
verification: Check firmware configuration and measure current and transitions under load.
limitations: STM32 guidance is not a universal unused-pin rule for other MCUs; analog mode, tolerance and reset defaults vary.
